title: The challenge
html:
01 / The challenge

Time-critical decisions.
Data in different places.

The Border Trade Matching Service (BTMS) was a new internal service designed to replace a legacy system. Border and operational staff needed to make accurate, time-critical decisions on goods entering the UK from the EU and the rest of the world.

The service needed to bring together data from HMRC’s Customs Declaration Service (CDS) and IPAFFS, helping staff identify mismatches, understand why goods might be held and resolve issues to keep the border flowing.

title: The design
html:
02 / The design

Find it. Understand it. Act on it.

As Lead interaction designer, I designed a search-led interface and clear results views, with visual indicators and filters to help staff identify discrepancies and prioritise action.

Make the sequence visible.

I designed a consignment timeline to show key events, decisions and status changes over time, alongside clearer system messaging and errors to support issue resolution.

Support the wider operation.

I also designed the BTMS reporting service, using graphs to show trends and operational data. Accessibility and GOV.UK compliance informed the work, including WCAG-aligned patterns and accessible data visualisation.

title: Outcome
html:
04 / Outcome

A clearer basis for action.

The resulting service made it easier for border teams to identify issues, understand what had happened and take the right action.

One place to find consignments, inspect matched information and follow the events behind their status.
